newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China resells small U.S. soymeal cargo - HK traders.
newsitem.headline: China resells small U.S. soymeal cargo - HK traders.

text.p: One small cargo of U.S. origin soymeal was resold by China a few days ago and talk of China cancelling or reselling 450,000 tonnes of meal purchase contracts was exaggerated, traders in Hong Kong said on Monday.
"As far as our company goes, one small cargo of U.S. origin soymeal was washed out a few days ago," said a source at an international trading house.

Domestic meal prices were still at about 2,700 yuan ($325) per tonne, equivalent to about $290 per tonne, C&F China, so Chinese end-users could resell the meal on the international market for a profit of about $8.00-9.00 a tonne, the source said.

Chicago Board of Trade soybean and soymeal futures fell on Friday on widespread talk that China had cancelled recent soymeal purchases of 450,000 tonnes, mostly from South America and India. March soymeal closed $1.80 a tonne lower at $257.60.
Other Hong Kong and China-based traders said although it was very likely that China had cancelled or resold previously bought meal contracts, 450,000 tonnes seemed like a very large quantity.
Chinese end-users were becoming traders themselves, said several traders.
"They watch the international markets and ask agents to resell on their behalf," said one Hong Kong trader.
The weather had eased in southern China and ports were not as congested, traders said on Monday.
One Beijing-based source estimated total storage capacity at Chinese ports to be around 400,000 tonnes and estimated that they would reach capacity by the end of March. This could not be confirmed.
Traders said they remained optimistic about long term Chinese demand for feed meal and said China would continue to buy if prices were around $280 per tonne, C&F China.
"At the moment, there is still about $10-15 difference in meal," said one trader. He said the level was too expensive for buyers. -- Mishi Saran (852) 2843 6358
